hold_text: Tier-3 order path. The diff changes what instruction reaches the venue on an Alpaca close: src/units/accounts/execute.py is named in this guard's own TIER3_PATHS, and src/units/accounts/alpaca_client.py is Tier-2 by the src/** rule. The operation change itself IS approved — the operator was asked on 2026-09-08 whether to trade-scope the Alpaca close or rule whole-symbol close intended, and chose to trade-scope it. What needs a human read is the CONFIRMATION, which the approval did not settle, and it needs reading in two separate parts because collapsing them is how a default drifts across two venues. (1) THE PARTIAL-FILL RULE IS `strict`, AND THAT IS NOT A NEW CHOICE: a reduction that lands only partly (10 of a requested 16) does NOT confirm — retCode 1, the row stays open, the monitor retries. That is the same answer the operator gave for IB on #11279, for the reason recorded there ('erring toward a phantom OPEN row that existing reconcilers clean up, rather than a phantom CLOSED row that fabricates PnL on the remainder and leaves lots naked'), applied to the mirror venue rather than defaulted into. (2) THE MEASUREMENT IS WHAT IS GENUINELY OPEN FOR ALPACA. #11279's approval says in terms 'EXPLICITLY NOT Alpaca — Alpaca's mirror defect is decided separately on #11312', and that decision has not been made. Here the whole-symbol path KEEPS its strict 'the symbol must disappear' gate untouched, and only the NEW partial path measures the trade's own quantity delta — because a partial close can never satisfy a flatness gate and would otherwise report failure forever while retrying, eating the sibling's position a slice at a time. Loosening the measurement only for a path whose OPERATION was narrowed in the same commit is what keeps this from reinstating BL-20260707's false-SUCCESS; that ordering is the safety property and it is the thing to check. Holding is also right because this must not land ahead of a human reading the MI-140 coupling: alpaca_live is real money and immune today only because it cannot place orders at all.
why: Trade-scopes the Alpaca close OPERATION and modify_protective, under WO-20260908-TRADE-SCOPE-THE-ALPACA-CLOSE-OPERATION-AND, from MI-173's measurement in #11312. execute.close_open_position validated a per-trade qty and then never passed it, and AlpacaClient.close had no qty parameter at all, so closing a 16-share journal row on a symbol the account was short 72 of liquidated all 72 and left the sibling row open with nothing behind it. The first step was a capability question, not a patch: DELETE /v2/positions/{symbol_or_asset_id} documents a qty query parameter ('the number of shares to liquidate. Can accept up to 9 decimal points. Cannot work with percentage'), so the venue CAN express the scoped operation and the operator's approval holds. Scope is resolved from one live position read taken before anything destructive: a trade that IS the whole position keeps the pre-existing whole-symbol path byte-for-byte, a trade smaller than the position takes a reduction that cancels nothing, and an unreadable position DEFERS rather than falling back to a flatten. modify_protective gains the same qty scoping and REFUSES rather than guessing when no leg matches or two same-size legs are indistinguishable. The success log no longer prints a per-trade qty next to a whole-symbol flatten. It does NOT extend #11279's confirmation change to Alpaca, does not remediate MI-140, and does not touch account capability gating or config. TEST POPULATION, measured against main's src by exception TYPE rather than by counting reds: 18 tests, 16 failed, 2 passed, of which only SIX failures are BEHAVIOURAL. Those six go through execute.close_open_position / execute.modify_open_order, whose signatures are identical on both trees, so on main they run the defect and report it. TEN fail with TypeError because they hand the client a qty that has no parameter there — the absence of the feature, NOT a demonstration of the defect, and not counted as evidence. TWO pass on both trees and are the only true either-way controls. ⚠️ An earlier version of this field claimed ten behavioural failures; that was wrong in the flattering direction, and the fix was to the TESTS (three caller-level ones added) rather than to the wording. The split is restated in the test module's own docstring.
